frqPlan.focus: Two fictional historians interpret why the population and political influence of the South and Southwest grew after 1970: one emphasizes air conditioning, defense spending and lower taxes, the other emphasizes retirement migration and the decline of older industrial cities. Keep all rubric examples to well-established facts about air conditioning, military bases, federal highway and housing spending, and state tax policy; do not mention Medicare or Social Security.

Non-text source: a table (illustrative composite, labeled as such) of the number of miles of railroad track in operation in the North and in the South in 1850 and 1860, consistent with the Northern advantage in railroads before the Civil War; keep every acceptable answer to simple comparisons stated directly in the table.
